body:
selfhost/emit.prn now supports a raw string literal as a call argument (f "lit"), closing the no-literals half of a gap named since the very first binary-op/plain-call work. Found and fixed a real, live, silently-wrong-C bug while verifying: (f (and b b)) as a call argument was silently emitting f(and(b, b)) -- a call to a never-defined function -- since plain-call-shaped? never excluded or/and/not the way alloc/binary-ops already are, a collision only reachable since the earlier nested-call-argument widening. Fixed with a new bool-op-symbol? exclusion. 6 new tests including a real compile+run+assert check. Zero regressions: 336-test suite + all 6 selfhost domains + bazel build/test clean. PARENA commit f5c2c3b.

⚓ ☃
title: Self-hosted compiler: string-literal-as-a-call-argument support + fixed a real and/or/not bug
